 Ajit Mishra, SVP – Research, Religare Broking 
 Markets remained under pressure on Friday, extending their losing streak to a fourth consecutive session amid rising crude oil prices and escalating geopolitical tensions. Despite opening on a positive note, the benchmark indices reversed their early gains as selling pressure intensified through the session. The Nifty slipped below the 22,400 mark intraday, reflecting deteriorating investor sentiment and a lack of sustained buying support.
 On the sectoral front, IT stocks demonstrated relative resilience, supported by earnings-related optimism and buying interest in select technology heavyweights. However, weakness across most other sectors weighed on overall sentiment, with metal, realty and energy emerging among the major laggards. The sharp underperformance of midcap and smallcap stocks further highlighted heightened risk aversion and persistent selling pressure beyond frontline stocks.
 Among the key concerns, Brent crude approached $115 per barrel amid escalating tensions in the Middle East. For India, persistently high crude prices pose risks to imported inflation, corporate margins and currency stability. Continued foreign fund outflows and uncertainty across global markets further dampened risk appetite, adding to the challenges facing domestic equities.
 After four consecutive sessions of decline, the Nifty has approached its key support zone of 22,200–22,400. A decisive break down below this range could open the door to further downside towards 21,700. Conversely, a sustained recovery above 22,900 could revive hopes of a rebound, potentially paving the way towards 23,300. Meanwhile, continued weakness in midcap and smallcap stocks is likely to keep market participants on their toes. We thus recommend traders maintain a cautious stance and prioritise disciplined risk management. Long-term investors, however, may selectively accumulate quality large-cap stocks in a staggered manner, keeping a medium- to long-term investment horizon.

A reasonable bear candle was formed with long lower shadow on the daily chart on Friday after the formation of Doji type candle pattern on Thursday.  Amol Athawale, VP Technical Research, Kotak Neo 
 In the last week, the benchmark indices witnessed selling pressure at higher levels. On weekly basis the Nifty ended 2.4 percent lower, while the Sensex was down by 1575 points. Among sectors, almost all the major sectoral indices registered selling pressure at higher level but Defence, Chemical, indices lost the most, shedding over 7 percent. During the week, the market slipped below the 23,000/74000 support level, and post-breakdown selling pressure intensified.
 Technically, the index formed a long bearish candle on the weekly charts, indicating further weakness from the current levels. We believe that the short-term market outlook remains weak; however, the possibility of a trend reversal from the current levels cannot be ruled out.
 For traders, the 20-day SMA (Simple Moving Average) or 22,700 for Nifty and for Sensex 73700 would act as an immediate resistance zone. If the market succeeds in trading above this level, we could expect a sharp pullback rally to 23,000–23,200/74000-74600. On the flip side, below the 20-day SMA, weak sentiment is likely to continue. Below this level, the market could retest 22,400–22,200/73400-72800.
 For Bank Nifty, the 20-day SMA or 55,000 would act as a trend-deciding level. Below this level, the index could slip to 53,500–53,200. On the flip side, above 55,000, it could move up to 55,500–55,800.

 The rise in India VIX also indicates that near-term volatility will persist. Continued Middle East tensions could keep crude prices high, while the AI-led global equity sell-off continues to weigh on risk appetite.
 Going forward, inflation trends and the response of major central banks in balancing inflation and growth will be critical to market direction. In this environment, we expect stock- and sector-specific opportunities to dominate, with earnings visibility and valuation comfort emerging as the key differentiators.
